workstream: W4-1c — Inventory population and demographic sources
scope: Official Philippine Statistics Authority sources only. This step inventories usable population/demographic series and geography constraints; it does not implement indicator data.
geographyRule: Prefer current 23-barangay Makati. Historical values are usable only when the official source explicitly restates/excludes the 10 barangays transferred to Taguig or when a current-boundary aggregate can be reproduced from canonical barangay observations.

officialSources.title: City of Makati — Philippine Standard Geographic Code
officialSources.note: Use barangays.ts as the canonical Makati barangay identity layer; do not duplicate the 23 population values inside Statistics.

officialSources.title: Population and Annual Population Growth Rate based on the 2010, 2015, 2020 and 2024 censuses
usableFor: annual population growth rates between census periods
officialSources.geography: HUC/city series; Makati is explicitly footnoted as excluding the 10 barangays transferred to Taguig.
officialSources.note: This is the preferred historical city population series because the source explicitly handles the Makati/Taguig boundary break.

officialSources.title: Total Population, Household Population, and Number of Households by Province, City, Municipality, and Barangay as of 01 July 2024 — NCR
usableFor: 2024 number of households by current barangay
city totals derived from the current 23 barangays
officialSources.geography: NCR city/municipality/barangay. The source separately identifies transferred Embo barangays under Taguig.
officialSources.note: This is the strongest candidate for expanding BetterBarangay statistics beyond total population while preserving canonical barangay scope.

officialSources.title: Total Population, Household Population, Number of Households and Average Household Size by Region, Province, and Highly Urbanized City: Philippines, 2024
officialSources.geography: HUC/city; Makati current-boundary treatment follows the 2024 POPCEN transfer notes.
officialSources.note: For citywide average household size, prefer the published PSA value. Barangay average household size may be explicitly derived from household population / household count if needed.

officialSources.title: Household Population by Age-Group, Region, Province, and Highly Urbanized City: Philippines, 2024 Census of Population
usableFor: 2024 Makati household population by age group
age/sex shares derived from published counts
officialSources.geography: HUC/city only. The table explicitly footnotes Makati as excluding the 10 transferred barangays.
officialSources.note: Do not imply barangay-level age/sex detail from this HUC-level table.

officialSources.title: Population, Land Area, Population Density, and Percent Change in Population Density: 2015, 2020, and 2024
officialSources.geography: HUC/city. Makati is explicitly footnoted as excluding the 10 transferred barangays.
officialSources.note: Prefer this current-boundary density series over older publications whose Makati land area/population may reflect the former 33-barangay city.

officialSources.title: Population of Legislative Districts based on the 2024 Census of Population
officialSources.geography: 2024 legislative-district geography; official release identifies Makati as having two districts and reports the Second District at 40,444 persons.
officialSources.note: Useful for Government/Elections/BetterBarangay context, but not a priority headline Statistics indicator. Import only from the full official table, not by subtracting one district from the city total.

officialSources.title: 2024 Census of Population statistical tables
officialSources.note: Use the specific table/matrix as the indicator source whenever possible; keep this page as the release index.

officialSources.title: Countryside in Figures / City of Makati profile using 2020 CPH
officialSources.geography: Former Makati geography including the transferred barangays; the profile reports 2020 household population on the old city boundary.
officialSources.note: Do not use its citywide age/sex or household totals as comparable current-Makati values. A legacy table may be used only if explicitly labeled historical-33 or if current 23-barangay values can be reconstructed from sufficiently granular official observations.

candidateIndicators.ownerPattern: city indicator derived/reference + canonical barangay data
published city value; explicit derived barangay value if shown

candidateIndicators.note: All current Makati barangays are classified Urban in PSGC; this is more useful as geography metadata than as a headline metric.
Authoritative 2024 release exists, but it is lower priority than household/age/sex indicators for the first implementation batch.
Old-boundary city totals cannot be mixed with current-boundary Makati.

comparabilityRules: The 2010/2015/2020/2024 city population trend may be used only from a PSA series that explicitly excludes the 10 transferred barangays for Makati.
Never use the old 629,616-style 2020 city total or its associated demographic tables as current-boundary Makati without an explicit historical-33 label.
Do not derive missing barangay demographic detail from a city/HUC table.
A city total may be derived from canonical barangay observations only when all 23 current barangays are present for the same indicator, period and definition.
Average household size may be derived only from household population divided by household count for the same geography/period; missing counts are not zero.
Legislative-district population must come from the official district table, not subtraction from the city total.
If PSA issues an erratum/revision, the indicator revision metadata must retain the previous version/date and point to the revised source.

implementationBatchRecommendation.rationale: This batch materially broadens the current Statistics product while keeping every implemented value on an explicit current-boundary or current-barangay basis.

crossFunctionReuse.use: 2024 household population, household count and explicitly derived household size by canonical barangay where the official table supplies the inputs.
Legislative-district population only if imported from the full official district table.
Reports should reference indicator IDs and dated values rather than becoming a second demographic datastore.
No demographic count is derived from Place Registry. Future place links may contextualize a sourced indicator but do not establish demographic denominators.
Map implemented indicator families to relevant BetterGov national-data/visualization resources and BetterLGU comparison destinations during W4-5 cross-linking; keep PSA as the visible primary source.

nextStep.title: Inventory economic and business indicators
nextStep.maximumScope: Official-source research only for GDP/economic structure, establishments/employment/business indicators that can be stated consistently.
